title: Grants linking three filers in a closed loop
question: Which three organizations reported cash grants from A to B, B to C and C to A during exactly the same tax period?
finding: 2,311 latest Form 990 filings yielded 26,352 positive cash-grant entries with a different recipient EIN. They contain 9 three-organization cycles across 8 distinct directed groups. Distinct groups recurring in more than one period: 1.
how: Read the grantor EIN from the return header and the recipient EIN, cash amount and purpose from each Schedule I entry. Require all three returns to have identical start and end dates. Count rotations of a group once. Each table row names the XML file inside the linked IRS download.
limits: The sample covers targeted filers with saved electronic returns. 0 selected latest Form 990 returns had no XML on disk. Filing periods do not reveal the order of payments. Coalition work, fiscal sponsorship and separate restricted projects can produce these patterns. A transaction ledger, award agreement and bank reference would be needed to trace the same dollars or show that a City award funded an onward grant. Schedule I, Part II requires an itemized recipient entry when a domestic organization or government receives more than $5,000 in total grants or assistance from the filer during the tax year. Smaller grants may be absent. Under the IRS instructions, an accrual-basis filer following FASB ASC 958 reports the present value of a grant payable in future years. An amount in the cash-grant column therefore does not establish a transfer date.
